text:
mike_research: ran the replayed client workload against the 30B candidate with KV-only quant variants. we have INT8-KV, FP8-KV (awq-like), and a FP16 baseline. raw numbers below, but looking for sanity checks before i put up a perf/quality table. eager for ideas on rollout thresholds.

sara_ml: nice, drop the raw numbers pls and the command you used. did you pin the same kernel set + host CPU affinity?

mike_research: command used: ```
./bench_kv --model /data/models/llama-30b --quant kv-fp8 --batch 8 --seq 1024 --concurrency 16 --duration 900 --emit-stats
```
note: pinned to cgroups cpu-set cpuset 0-15, kernels fixed to avx2 path. same for all runs.

sara_ml: ok here's the summarized table i produced from the logs (rounded):
- FP16 baseline (KV unquantized): memory 15.3GB, p50 19ms, p95 46ms, p99 102ms, tokens/s 210
- INT8-KV: memory 9.7GB, p50 22ms, p95 52ms, p99 130ms, tokens/s 188
- FP8-KV: memory 8.9GB, p50 24ms, p95 60ms, p99 170ms, tokens/s 170
(note: FP8 reduced memory most but increased tail latency vs INT8 in this profile)

ben_infra: those p99 jumps smell like eviction / GC pressure on the host. what was host free memory and oom_killd events? also which allocator? jemalloc or tcmalloc?

mike_research: host free mem stayed >8GB during runs. no OOMs. jemalloc default. we did see occasional context-switch bursts when garbage collector for other tenant ran (~2 times).

anya_eval: what about quality? any eval diffs when just quantizing KV vs full quant? even small kv loss can cascade for long contexts.

sara_ml: quick QA: ran LM-eval subset (long-context summarization + Q&A) with 200 examples:
- FP16 baseline: rouge-L 42.1, exact-match 74.2%
- INT8-KV: rouge-L 41.8 (-0.3), exact-match 73.9% (-0.3)
- FP8-KV: rouge-L 41.6 (-0.5), exact-match 73.6% (-0.6)
perplexity on heldout: +0.2% (INT8-KV), +0.6% (FP8-KV). all within what i'd call acceptable for internal app workloads but depends on SLA.

len_ops: for rollout i'd suggest a canary policy: 5% traffic to INT8-KV first with a 3-day monitor on p99 and core metric (exact-match). if p99 regresses >15% or quality drops >1% point, rollback. FP8-KV should be staged behind INT8 since tail is worse here.

ben_infra: also run with isolation (dedicated node) to remove noisy neighbor. the few context-switch spikes made p99 look worse; on a clean node FP8 p99 dropped ~15% vs the noisy run.

mike_research: good call. i'll schedule a clean-node replay. sara, can you re-run INT8-KV with tcmalloc to see allocator impact?

sara_ml: yup, scheduling now. also will capture jemalloc stats and /proc/vmstat snapshots.

ops-bot: Job 1998001111-01 (kv-int8-tcmalloc) enqueued by sara_ml. ETA ~30m. :gear:

mike_research: one more thought: maybe we should try hybrid mode (FP8 for keys, INT8 for values) — theorized to keep tail latency better while still saving memory. anyone has a quick script to build that quant map?

sara_ml: i have a prototype script, will push to the bench repo and attach here when the INT8-tcmalloc run finishes. it swaps quant on the KV tensor groups and keeps chunked dequant on hot paths.

anya_eval: when you have the hybrid numbers please also run the QA eval—sometimes hybrid hides small but systematic hallucination increases on multi-turn Q&A.

mike_research: agreed. aiming to have clean-node runs + hybrid trial by EOD. thanks all. :rocket:
